uncited: What sets it apart from its siblings is the specific handling of mesh primitives: [Soft Rasterizer](6779-soft-rasterizer.md) and [Generalized Differentiable Renderer (GenDR)](11684-generalized-differentiable-renderer-gendr.md) focus on probabilistic or generalized soft rasterization, while [Stochastic Opacity Masking](20635-stochastic-opacity-masking.md) addresses stochastic visibility; differentiable mesh rendering encompasses both rasterization-based approaches (like OpenDR, NMR, PyTorch3D) and physically-based ray-tracing approaches (like Mitsuba 2, nvdiffrast) that operate on explicit mesh geometry.
The core mechanism involves transforming the discrete, non-differentiable operations of standard rendering into continuous, differentiable functions.
**Soft Rasterization / Probabilistic Visibility:** Instead of hard occlusion tests, pixels are assigned a probabilistic occupancy based on the mesh's distance or coverage.
Renderers that wrap standard rasterization or ray-tracing pipelines in AD-compatible computation graphs.
Methods that derive explicit formulas for the gradient of the rasterization operation, particularly for visibility changes.
Techniques that render probabilistic maps of mesh triangles to allow gradient flow to occluded vertices.
High-performance implementations optimized for deep learning frameworks.
